title: Code Documentation Generator — LLM-Powered Code Intelligence System
text:
🧩 The Problem
Software documentation is often incomplete, inconsistent, or entirely missing. While large language models can generate summaries, they introduce critical challenges in real-world applications:

Hallucinated or incorrect content

Unstable formatting

Non-deterministic outputs

Difficulty parsing large or complex codebases

This project addresses the need for a reliable, structured system that can automatically generate high-quality documentation from source code while maintaining consistency and control.

title: Code Documentation Generator — LLM-Powered Code Intelligence System
text:
⚙️ My Approach
I designed a production-oriented NLP pipeline that integrates LLM generation into a deterministic system.

🏗 System Architecture
The system follows a modular architecture:

Streamlit UI (user interaction & file upload)

Renderer layer (orchestration and chunking)

LLM client (schema-constrained generation)

Prompt layer (hallucination control and formatting stability)

This separation of concerns ensures scalability, reliability, and maintainability. :contentReferenceoaicite:0



🧠 Key Design Components

1. Schema-Constrained Generation

Enforced structured outputs using JSON Schema

Ensured consistent formatting and valid outputs

Reduced hallucination and parsing errors



2. Hierarchical Summarization Pipeline

Stage 1: File-level structured summaries

Stage 2: Project-level aggregation

This improves coherence and scalability for large codebases.


3. Syntax-Aware Chunking (AST-Based)

Used Python AST parsing to preserve code structure

Avoided splitting functions or classes mid-block

Ensured semantically meaningful input to LLM



4. Hallucination Mitigation

Strict prompt constraints

“Do NOT invent APIs” rules

JSON-only output enforcement



5. Robust Fallback Strategy

Primary: OpenAI LLM generation

Fallback: Deterministic placeholder generation

This ensures the system never fails even when API is unavailable. :contentReferenceoaicite:1

title: Code Documentation Generator — LLM-Powered Code Intelligence System
text:
📊 Key Results

Built a fully functional system that converts raw code into structured documentation

Ensured stable and consistent outputs through schema enforcement

Maintained usability even under API failures (graceful degradation)

Delivered an interactive UI supporting file upload, preview, and export

title: Code Documentation Generator — LLM-Powered Code Intelligence System
text:
💡 Reflections

What I Learned

LLM systems require strict structure and constraints to be reliable

Schema enforcement is critical for production-grade generative AI

Multi-stage pipelines improve scalability and output quality

Defensive engineering is essential when integrating LLMs

This project shifted my perspective from prompt-based experimentation → system-level design thinking.



Limitations

Documentation quality depends on source code clarity

Very large projects may require performance optimization

Strict schemas limit expressive flexibility

Cannot infer undocumented business logic




Next Steps

Improve documentation richness while maintaining structure

Support additional programming languages

Add version-aware documentation updates

Integrate into enterprise developer workflows

title: Semantic Search & RAG System for Medical Literature
text:
The Problem
Medical research papers are information-dense, terminology-heavy, and difficult to navigate with traditional keyword search alone. Users often need not just document retrieval, but grounded answers to natural-language questions based on relevant evidence.
This project addressed that challenge by building a semantic search and RAG system for medical literature, designed to help users retrieve relevant papers and generate evidence-grounded answers from a corpus of more than 100 medical research papers.

title: Semantic Search & RAG System for Medical Literature
text:
My Approach
I designed and implemented an end-to-end NLP pipeline with a modular architecture:

PDF text extraction and cleaning
Paragraph-based chunking
SentenceTransformer embeddings
Cosine-similarity retrieval
Optional RAG answer generation via OpenAI
CLI and Streamlit interfaces

The system was designed with several production-oriented decisions:

Paragraph-level chunking to preserve semantic coherence
Length-bounded chunks to reduce noisy or overly sparse representations
Doc-level deduplication to prevent one source from dominating top results
Keyword prefilter with fallback to improve precision in heterogeneous corpora
Strict prompting constraints to reduce hallucination in answer generation

title: Semantic Search & RAG System for Medical Literature
text:
Key Results
The final system enabled users to:

Perform semantic search over 100+ medical papers
Retrieve top-K relevant documents using dense embeddings and cosine similarity
Ask natural-language questions and receive grounded answers
Interact through both a command-line interface and a Streamlit web app

Manual retrieval evaluation across domain-specific queries showed that:

Top-K results aligned well with domain concepts
Doc-level deduplication improved evidence diversity
Keyword prefilter improved precision for heterogeneous biomedical topics

title: Semantic Search & RAG System for Medical Literature
text:
Reflections

What I Learned
This project strengthened my ability to:

Build an end-to-end NLP system from raw documents to LLM output
Apply embeddings for real-world information retrieval
Design RAG pipelines with hallucination control
Think beyond assignment requirements toward production-ready architecture

It also deepened my understanding of the trade-offs between retrieval quality, chunk granularity, system modularity, and answer grounding.


Limitations

No OCR support for scanned PDFs
Biomedical-specific embedding models could further improve domain alignment
Cross-encoder reranking could improve retrieval precision
Citation granularity could be improved to link answers to exact PDF page locations



Next Steps
If I continue this project, I would focus on:

Adding PDF page-level citation linking
Testing biomedical-specific embedding models such as PubMedBERT
Adding cross-encoder reranking for more precise retrieval
Expanding evaluation with a more formal benchmark framework

title: Gemini PolicyPal — AI-Powered Insurance Policy Analyzer
text:
The Problem
Insurance policy documents are often long, complex, and difficult to interpret. Users struggle to quickly understand coverage details, identify exclusions, or compare multiple policies. Traditional keyword search is insufficient for navigating unstructured legal text, and manual comparison is time-consuming and error-prone.
This creates a need for an intelligent system that can: - Understand policy documents semantically
- Answer user questions accurately
- Compare multiple policies in a structured way

title: Gemini PolicyPal — AI-Powered Insurance Policy Analyzer
text:
My Approach
To address this problem, I built an end-to-end AI system based on a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline.

Document Processing

Parsed uploaded insurance documents (PDF/text)
Split documents into structured chunks
Cleaned and standardized text for downstream processing



Semantic Retrieval

Generated embeddings for each chunk

Implemented similarity-based retrieval to identify relevant content

Enabled context-aware search beyond keyword matching



RAG Question Answering

Retrieved top relevant chunks

Constructed grounded prompts for LLM

Generated answers strictly based on source content to reduce hallucination



Policy Comparison System

Designed a multi-document comparison module

Enabled side-by-side analysis of Policy A vs Policy B

Highlighted differences in coverage, exclusions, and conditions



User Interface

Built an interactive Streamlit app

Supported multi-file upload

Enabled real-time question answering and comparison

What I Learned

RAG pipelines are highly effective for grounding LLM responses in real data

Embedding-based retrieval significantly improves understanding of unstructured text

Designing reliable AI systems requires controlling hallucination and enforcing structure



Limitations

Performance depends on document quality and formatting

Long documents may require more advanced chunking strategies

No domain-specific fine-tuning (e.g., insurance-specific models)



Next Steps

Add citation highlighting (show exact source location)

Improve comparison visualization (UI enhancement)

Explore domain-specific embeddings for higher accuracy
